title: Nervous system: male anatomy
description: Male nervous-system overview with focused pelvic nerve notes for prostate, penis and perineum; tiny branches are not falsely pinned on a full-body image.

questions.question: Is the male nervous system built differently from the female nervous system?
questions.answer: The main brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerve plan is shared. A male-focused pelvic view highlights branches serving the prostate, penis and scrotum rather than implying separate male brain or spinal pathways.

questions.question: Which nerves contribute to penile erection?
questions.answer: Autonomic cavernous nerves arising from the prostatic plexus influence penile smooth muscle and blood flow. Somatic sensation from the penis is carried largely through the dorsal nerve of the penis, a pudendal branch.

questions.question: What is the pudendal nerve in the male pelvis?
questions.answer: The pudendal nerve derives from sacral segments S2–S4 and supplies much of the perineum. Its branches include the inferior rectal, perineal and dorsal penile nerves; these are distinct from pelvic autonomic nerves.

questions.question: How do pelvic splanchnic nerves differ from hypogastric nerves?
questions.answer: Pelvic splanchnic nerves carry sacral parasympathetic fibers from S2–S4 into pelvic plexuses. Hypogastric nerves convey predominantly sympathetic pathways from higher plexuses; both contribute to pelvic organ innervation.

questions.question: Can the full-body male nerve picture show individual cavernous nerves?
questions.answer: No. It is an orientation image for major nervous-system routes. Cavernous and prostatic plexus branches are described as unpinned study structures rather than falsely marked on a whole-body plate.
